t: LeetCode 3221 – Maximum Array Hopping Score II
o: Start at index 0, hop strictly rightward to the last index; each hop i→j earns (j − i) · nums[j]; maximize the total. Key structural insight: a hop's gain decomposes per unit step — every position p between i+1 and j contributes nums[j]. So the total equals Σ_p nums[nextHopTarget(p)], and it is optimal to always jump from the current index straight to the maximum element of the remaining suffix (exchange argument: paying any step to anything smaller than the suffix max can be improved). Both examples confirm: [1,5,8] → jump 0→2 for 16; [4,5,2,8,9,1,3] → 0→4→6 for 36 + 6 = 42.
k: Rewrite the score as a per-position payment to the target of the hop covering that position.
Greedy: repeatedly jump to the argmax of the untouched suffix; precompute suffix argmaxes for O(n).

a.i: Precompute best[i] = index of the maximum in nums[i..n-1]. From the current index i, hop to j = best[i+1], add (j − i) · nums[j], and repeat until reaching n − 1. Each hop lands on the best possible payer for the stretch it covers.
s: Fill best[] from right to left.
Walk i = 0; while i < n-1: j = best[i+1]; ans += (j-i)*nums[j]; i = j.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def maxScore(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        best = [0] * n
        best[n - 1] = n - 1
        for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
            best[i] = i if nums[i] > nums[best[i + 1]] else best[i + 1]
        ans = 0
        i = 0
        while i < n - 1:
            j = best[i + 1]
            ans += (j - i) * nums[j]
            i = j
        return ans

a.t: O(n) — one backward pass and one forward walk

a.i: dp[i] = best score to go from i to the end: dp[i] = max over j > i of (j − i)·nums[j] + dp[j], with dp[n−1] = 0. This makes the optimality structure explicit but costs O(n²), which can be slow at n = 10^5; it is mainly valuable as the stepping stone to discovering the greedy.
s: Iterate i from n−2 down to 0.
Try every landing j > i and take the best (j−i)·nums[j] + dp[j].
a.t: O(n²) — every (i, j) pair evaluated; may TLE at n = 10^5

w: Lead with the suffix-max greedy and justify it via the per-step decomposition — interviewers love the reframing. Pitfalls: the tempting 'monotonic stack of next-greater' shortcuts fail on cases like example 2; use 64-bit accumulation (score up to ~10^10); ensure the walk terminates at exactly n − 1. Follow-ups: minimum-score hopping, or hops restricted to bounded length (then a sliding-window maximum applies).
